definitions.explanation: Describes a claim or expression that overstates the truth, making something seem greater or better than it really is. Carries a critical, negative tone.

examples.japanese: {誇大|こだい}な{表現|ひょうげん}を{避|さ}ける。
その{広告|こうこく}は{誇大|こだい}だと{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: That advertisement was criticized as exaggerated.

examples.japanese: {誇大|こだい}な{宣伝|せんでん}に{惑|まど}わされて{高|たか}い{商品|しょうひん}を{買|か}ってしまった。
examples.english: Misled by exaggerated advertising, I ended up buying an expensive product.

notes:
Used as a na-adjective ({誇大|こだい}な) and in fixed compounds. Always carries a critical nuance of overstatement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {誇大|こだい}{広告|こうこく}: false/misleading advertising
- {誇大|こだい}{表現|ひょうげん}: exaggerated expression
- {誇大|こだい}{妄想|もうそう}: delusions of grandeur; megalomania

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大|おお}げさ: exaggerated — everyday and conversational
- {過大|かだい}: excessive; overestimated — emphasizes "too much" rather than boastful overstatement
